- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward by 2–5% if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- If sentiment shows strong negative drift (e.g., 0.0–0.4 over 3+ days), model overcorrects downward; avoid sharp drops below 70–72; consider mean reversion to prior 5-day average.
- Model underestimates prices when sentiment is weak or mixed (0.0–0.6) and recent price is falling; add 1–2% to forecast to account for lagged sentiment effect.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts early in the window (first 5–7 days); apply a 1–3% downward bias to first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is high but price is falling (e.g., +1.0 sentiment, -10% price drop), model may misread trend; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment-weighted mean of recent 7 days.
